key_status: outline only; exact source passages and expert review pending

required_evidence: Classify each system by mass, heat, and work crossing its boundary.
Relate an open control volume to practical equipment with flowing streams.
Retain the source's boundary and sign-convention context.
items.locator: DOE-THERMO-V1, PDF pages 79-85 (printed HT-01 pages 53-59), especially control-volume discussion on PDF pages 80-85
must_not_claim: Every process unit is necessarily steady state or adiabatic.

required_evidence: Identify internal or enthalpy, kinetic, potential, heat, work, and flow contributions applicable to the stated balance.
Distinguish steady state from assumptions that make individual terms negligible.
Preserve units, reference state, boundary, and sign convention.
items.locator: DOE-THERMO-V1, PDF pages 79-94 (printed HT-01 pages 53-68); energy forms on PDF page 85 and worked balances on pages 86-93
must_not_claim: Kinetic and potential energy are always negligible.

required_evidence: State that an equilibrium system responds in a direction that minimizes an applied stress.
Keep concentration, pressure, and temperature effects conditional on the reaction and system.
Explicitly distinguish equilibrium position from reaction kinetics.
items.locator: DOE-CHEM-V1, PDF page 58 (printed CH-01 page 36); NIST-KINETICS welcome snapshot, rate-record fields 1-7
must_not_claim: A thermodynamically favored shift proves the reaction will be fast.

required_evidence: Retain rate parameters and the stated mathematical rate form.
Retain temperature range, pressure range, bulk gas, data type, uncertainty, and experimental method when available.
Treat validity outside reported conditions as unresolved rather than silently extrapolating.
items.locator: NIST-KINETICS welcome snapshot, numbered description of rate-record fields 1-7
must_not_claim: One database rate expression is universally valid at all temperatures and pressures.

required_evidence: Differentiate molecular conduction, bulk-fluid convection, and electromagnetic radiation.
Retain the applicable temperature difference, geometry, area, material or film property, and boundary-condition dependence.
State that mode equations and coefficients do not alone complete exchanger or equipment design.
items.locator: DOE-HEAT-V2, PDF pages 24-28 (printed HT-02 pages 2-6) and radiant-transfer discussion on PDF page 48
must_not_claim: Only one heat-transfer mode can occur in a real process unit.

required_evidence: Describe laminar and turbulent flow behavior using the source terminology.
Explain Reynolds number as a dimensionless classification criterion based on inertial and viscous effects.
Retain geometry and transition-region limitations.
items.locator: DOE-FLOW-V3, PDF pages 39-42 (printed HT-03 pages 17-20); Reynolds definition and ranges on PDF pages 41-42
must_not_claim: One exact Reynolds-number cutoff applies to every geometry and disturbance level.

required_evidence: Identify pipe length, diameter, roughness or friction factor, velocity or flow, fluid properties, and fittings or local losses as applicable.
Separate distributed friction loss from local component loss.
Require numeric inputs, units, and a stated correlation or model for a final calculation.
items.locator: DOE-FLOW-V3, PDF pages 53-58 (printed HT-03 pages 31-36); Darcy equation and minor-loss summary
must_not_claim: A qualitative factor list is a calculated pressure drop.

required_evidence: Relate membrane or barrier permeability and pressure driving force to process gas transport.
Describe separation performance using the source's stated factor or stage context.
Retain equipment construction, operating-condition, and model limitations.
items.locator: DOE-CHEM-V1 Appendix A, PDF pages 83-91 (printed pages A-5 through A-13), including design versus actual permeability
must_not_claim: A qualitative permeability statement is sufficient to design an industrial separation cascade.

required_evidence: Describe exchange of dissolved ions with functional sites on a resin.
Describe exhaustion and regeneration without inventing reagent conditions.
Retain feed composition, capacity, selectivity, competing ions, pretreatment, and waste-handling limitations when supported.
items.locator: DOE-CHEM-V2, PDF pages 63-70 (printed CH-04 pages 7-14) and malfunction/temperature limitations on PDF pages 78-83
must_not_claim: Ion exchange removes every contaminant from every water stream.

required_evidence: Retain chemical identity, concentration, physical state, exposure route, incompatibilities, conditions, and source-stated controls or warnings.
Separate source-grounded screening information from task-specific risk assessment and procedure development.
State missing facility, quantity, equipment, ventilation, and regulatory context as evidence gaps.
items.locator: DOE-CHEM-V2, PDF page 96, General Safety Precautions; source states precautions are not all-inclusive and requires chemical-specific MSDS consultation
must_not_claim: A general handbook paragraph is a complete task-specific operating procedure.
